extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and investigators preparing NIH grant applications (e.g., R01, R03, R21, K, F, SBIR/STTR) who are new to grant writing or seeking examples of funded applications.
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using NIH sample grant applications and related materials when preparing and drafting NIH funding applications; emphasizes following current instructions, seeking feedback, and consulting NIH staff. Useful for applicants across common NIH mechanisms (R01, R03, R21, K, F, SBIR/STTR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the current funding opportunity announcement and application instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and carefully follow the instructions in the funding opportunity announcement (FOA) to which you are responding and the current application instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and instructions change regularly; the sample applications were developed using the application forms and instructions in effect at the time of their submission, so do not assume the examples match current required formats or content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat sample applications as illustrative examples, not prescriptive templates
rubrics_metrics.description: The best way to present your science may differ substantially from the approach taken by those who wrote the example applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sample applications to learn organization, level of detail, and presentation approaches, but adapt structure and emphasis to the current FOA and to what best presents your specific science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek feedback on your draft application from mentors and others
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain critical review and input on your draft application from mentors, colleagues, and other experienced reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback helps ensure clarity, competitiveness, and that your presentation aligns with review expectations; do not rely solely on example applications or assumptions about reviewer priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult an NIH program officer for programmatic advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to an NIH program officer in your area of science for advice about the best type of grant program and the Institute or Center that might be interested in your idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A program officer can provide guidance on fit to FOAs, appropriate grant mechanisms, and may advise on strengthening the application; contact them early in concept development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use agency-provided sample repositories (e.g., NIAID's Sample Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review available collections of funded applications, summary statements, and plans (e.g., NIAID’s Sample Applications and More) to see examples of successful submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These repositories are useful reference material for format, content level, and supporting documents, but always cross-check with current instructions and seek external feedback.
